findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the expected outcome of a local removal of an inbound-origin release (no Jira write; inbound re-adds it, or otherwise), and pin it in the round-trip test or document it as a known limit alongside the compaction limit
evidence: "`source == "inbound"` deltas are skipped and `.removed` is never folded"

AC only covers "Removing a locally added release"
findings.finding: The plan never states what happens when a user locally removes a release that arrived from Jira (inbound-origin). Such a name is never in intent, because inbound deltas are skipped and `.removed` is never folded. The outbound diff therefore will not remove it from Jira, and the next inbound pass will presumably re-add it locally. The plan neither states nor tests whether this revert is intended ADR 0124 behavior or a limitation to document.
scenarios: Jira sets fixVersion 2.3, which syncs inbound. A rebar user removes 2.3. No Jira write happens, and 2.3 reappears locally on the next pass.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the intended behavior for a persistent 4xx on a fixVersions write (keep retrying each pass vs back off or skip), and whether a logged write failure should trip the silent-no-op canary; add a test for the chosen behavior
evidence: "failures logged to stderr ... and retried next pass"
"computed > 0 with applied 0 trips the silent-no-op canary"
Docs: "the version must already exist in the Jira project, and Fix versions may need to be on the project's edit screen"
findings.finding: Some write failures are permanent and will recur on every pass: the version does not exist in the Jira project, or Fix versions is not on the edit screen. The plan's only handling is "logged to stderr and retried next pass", which repeats the failing PUT forever, and "computed > 0 with applied 0 trips the silent-no-op canary", which fires every pass for a non-silent, logged failure. The plan does not say whether permanent 4xx errors should be distinguished from transient ones, nor what the operator-facing signal is.
scenarios: A user adds release "2.5" locally before anyone creates it in Jira. Every pass sends a doomed PUT, logs a 400, and trips the canary.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] In step 5, state the disposition per failure class for release writes: transient (429/5xx) is retryable next pass; permanent (400 missing version / field not editable) has a named surfaced outcome. State how the silent-no-op canary behaves on a repeated permanent failure, and add a dispatch test for the missing-version 400.
evidence: "per item, failures logged to stderr (for `urllib.error.HTTPError`, with up to 500 bytes of Jira's error body) and retried next pass"
"the version must already exist in the Jira project, and Fix versions may need to be on the project's edit screen"
"computed > 0 with applied 0 trips the silent-no-op canary"
findings.finding: The new per-item dispatch failure arm in `_update_one_dispatch_releases` gives every failure one disposition: 'failures logged to stderr ... and retried next pass'. It never classifies failures as transient (e.g. 429 or 5xx, retryable) or permanent. Permanent cases include a 400 because the version does not exist in the Jira project, or because Fix versions is not on the edit screen — both of which the plan's own docs note predicts. A permanent rejection will therefore be re-attempted and logged on every pass indefinitely. The plan also does not say whether the silent-no-op canary ('computed > 0 with applied 0 trips the silent-no-op canary') then fires on every pass for the same stuck item, or what the operator sees.
scenarios: A local release '2.5' that was never created as a Jira version gets a 400 on every reconcile pass. That produces repeated stderr noise and a canary trip each pass, with no terminal or operator-actionable disposition.
A transient 503 and a permanent 400 are indistinguishable to the caller, so neither monitoring nor the canary can tell 'will self-heal' from 'needs a human'.

findings.finding: The plan names two Jira-side preconditions for the write: the version must exist in the project, and the field must be on the edit screen. Neither is checked before writing, and the plan gives no handling for the predictable rejection when either is unmet. Step 5 treats every failure as 'logged to stderr ... and retried next pass'. So a name the project lacks, or a project without Fix versions on its screen, causes a 400 that repeats on every pass and never resolves. ADR 0124 decision 8 handles exactly this gap (one per-pass project version read, plus withhold-and-alert). This plan neither implements it nor names the sibling child that does.
